L31·N4052unmasked layer
This neuron has no clean lexical or structural trigger — it fires diffusely and at low-to-moderate levels across mid-sentence content words in casual first-person blog/travel prose (peaks land on arbitrary tokens like a year digit, " Display", " vent(uring)", " source", " on", a sentence-final period), and is strongly suppressed on other ordinary tokens (" lemon", " to", ",", " gaining"), so it looks like a broad context/style detector rather than a specific-token detector.

L31·N7448unmasked layer
Weakly/diffusely tuned, mostly-function-word neuron in low-quality web/SEO/boilerplate prose: it fires on generic filler tokens — second-person "you/You/US", prepositions like " where", and digits beginning a year — while being most strongly *suppressed* by similar function words (" for", " a", " you") in the same kind of marketing/how-to text, so it looks more like a polysemantic filler-token detector than a semantic feature.

L31·N10187unmasked layer
Fires on "continuation" tokens in the middle of rigid, formulaic sequences — e.g. a repeated first name inside a long list of names, the comma between authors in a citation, the "/" in a ratio like t/tp, a syllable in a hyphenated phonetic spelling — i.e. a mid-item token where the pattern's continuation is highly constrained rather than any one semantic topic.
